trials.summary: Trial 1 (target rule, h_f 5.349, h_s 7.652) scores objective 0.0837 ± 0.0211 with gamma finite on all 8 cells and no divergence, clearing the success bar but sitting just above exp6's 0.0803.
trials.key_insight: Pushing the winning target rule from exp6's h_f 4.0 up to 5.35 (and h_s 3.675 -> 7.65) does not improve the objective (0.0803 -> 0.0837), the first sign of a turnover above exp6's optimum.

trials.summary: Trial 2 (sim rule, h_f 5.308, h_s 3.060) scores objective 0.1249 ± 0.0398 with gamma finite and no divergence, far worse than trial_01 (0.0837) because gamma collapses in all four low-count cells.
trials.key_insight: The `sim` bandwidth rule is decisively inferior to `target` at comparable bandwidth: it drives gamma to 31-40 % of truth on the Trans05/Trans20 cells and lifts the objective from 0.0837 to 0.1249.

trials.summary: Trial 3 (power rule, h_f 8.658, h_s 4.220) scores objective 0.1541 ± 0.0791 with gamma finite and no divergence, the worst so far, driven by a mu overshoot of up to +123 % on the low-count cells.
trials.key_insight: The `power` rule is the worst of the three; with {target, sim, power} at comparable scale giving {0.0837, 0.1249, 0.1541}, the bandwidth RULE is a first-order lever and `target` is the clear front-runner.

trials.summary: Trial 4 (target rule, h_f 9.821, h_s 2.920) scores objective 0.0926 ± 0.0207, worse than trial_01 (0.0837), extending the target rule further above exp6's optimum on the wrong side.
trials.key_insight: On the target rule the objective rises monotonically with h_f above ~4 (0.0803 @4.0, 0.0837 @5.35, 0.0926 @9.82), so exp6's h_f = 4.0 already sat at the target-rule optimum and the extended upper bound buys nothing for this rule.

trials.summary: Trial 5 (target rule, h_f 3.580, h_s 5.784) scores objective 0.0818 ± 0.0239, a new campaign best, confirming the target rule is better just below exp6's h_f = 4.0 than above it.
trials.key_insight: Placing the target rule below exp6's bound (h_f 5.35 -> 3.58) improves the objective (0.0837 -> 0.0818), so the target-rule optimum lies around h_f ~3.6-4.0 and the exp6 ceiling was close to optimal for this rule.

trials.summary: Trial 6 (target rule, h_f 3.678, h_s 5.319), the highest-EI proposal, scores objective 0.0890 ± 0.0237, within sampling noise of the nearby best (trial_05 0.0818).
trials.key_insight: The target rule's objective is essentially flat/noise-limited across h_f ~3.5-5.4 (0.080-0.089, SE ~0.024), so further coefficient tuning of the target rule in that region does not reliably beat exp6's 0.0803.

trials.summary: Trial 7 (target rule, h_f 1.130, h_s 8.612) scores objective 0.1165 ± 0.0827, worse than the target plateau, failing via a mu overshoot up to +172.9 % on the low-count cells.
trials.key_insight: The target-rule optimum is now bracketed on both sides (worse at h_f 1.13 and at h_f 9.82, flat-best around h_f 3.5-5.5), so exp6's frozen h_f=4.0 is essentially the target-rule optimum.

trials.summary: Trial 8 (target rule, h_f 3.779, h_s 7.279) scores objective 0.0882 ± 0.0251, another plateau sample consistent with the flat 0.081-0.089 band around the target-rule optimum.
trials.key_insight: The target plateau now has five samples in 0.081-0.089 with no internal trend, confirming the objective in h_f ~3-5.5 is noise-flat and that exp6's 0.0803 is the best value the target rule reaches.

trials.summary: Trial 9 (target rule, h_f 4.045, h_s 7.567) scores objective 0.0859 ± 0.0210, a plateau sample that holds h_f at exp6's 4.0 while raising h_s, and is slightly worse than exp6 (0.0803).
trials.key_insight: Holding h_f at exp6's optimum but raising h_s (3.675 -> 7.567) costs 0.0803 -> 0.0859, a weak (within-SE) hint that a smaller sigma-channel coefficient is mildly better.

trials.summary: Trial 10 (target rule, h_f 4.698, h_s 7.535) scores objective 0.0831 ± 0.0200, a mid-plateau sample consistent with the flat 0.080-0.089 target band.
trials.key_insight: Seven plateau samples now span 0.0803-0.0890 with no internal trend, cementing that the target-rule objective is flat/noise-limited across h_f ~3.5-5.5 and that exp6's 0.0803 remains the best.

trials.summary: Trial 11 (target rule, h_f 5.061, h_s 2.518) scores objective 0.0873 ± 0.0268, showing the low-sigma-coefficient corner gives no improvement over the plateau.
trials.key_insight: Lowering h_s to 2.52 does not improve on exp6's 0.0803, so the target-rule plateau is flat in h_s as well as h_f and the objective there is entirely noise-limited.

trials.summary: Trial 12 (target rule, h_f 5.243, h_s 7.906) scores objective 0.0906 ± 0.0214, another sample from the flat target plateau.
trials.key_insight: Nine plateau samples now span 0.0803-0.0906 with no trend; the target-rule objective is flat/noise-limited across the whole tested band.

trials.summary: Trial 13 (target rule, h_f 5.203, h_s 7.962) scores objective 0.0904 ± 0.0196, the tenth sample from the flat target plateau.
trials.key_insight: The target plateau's ten samples span 0.0803-0.0906 with no coefficient trend, reinforcing that exp6's frozen target/4.0 point is as good as any on the plateau.

trials.summary: Trial 14 (target rule, h_f 5.207, h_s 7.786) scores objective 0.0920 ± 0.0218, the eleventh flat-plateau sample.
trials.key_insight: The target plateau's eleven samples span 0.0803-0.0920 with no coefficient trend, confirming once more that exp6's frozen point is representative of the best the target rule reaches.

trials.summary: Trial 15 (target rule, h_f 3.194, h_s 7.663) scores objective 0.0826 ± 0.0273, the best campaign sample since trial_05 and consistent with the flat target plateau.
trials.key_insight: The target plateau's twelve samples span 0.0803-0.0920 with no trend; the low-h_f half of the plateau is as good as the middle, and exp6's 0.0803 still stands as the best single value.

protocol.model: series-21 (17g) model on REAL data; mu reward = Anuar's per-run likelihood (MU_REWARD=loglik_mean), mu score denominator = per-experiment sigma_prop (MU_SCORE=sigma_prop)
protocol.question: experiment_7 - bandwidth RULE family campaign: the learning-rate schedule (exp5 winner) and the score design (exp6 winner: sigma_weight=0.865, gamma_rel_cap=0.107) are FROZEN; the campaign tunes the KDE bandwidth rule (target | sim | power) and its coefficients h_f_scale / h_s_scale extended to [1, 12].

frozen_schedule.note: experiment_5 winning trial (trial_21); the schedule is a plateau and is NOT searched here

frozen_score_design.note: experiment_6 winning trial (trial_07); the sigma-channel damping + gamma trust region are NOT searched here

protocol.no_clipping: CLIP = inf AND parameter clamps removed (mu/gamma unbounded)

divergence_guard.note: STOP the experiment and record diverged/diverged_at if a parameter leaves this band (guards the photon-count blow-up)

protocol.objective: T-weighted mean of CAP-capped per-cell rel-sq errors; err_i = min(rel_sq_i, CAP=1.0); w(T) = 0.25 + 0.75*T/100; objective = sum(w*err)/sum(w)

budget.held_out: 6 exps (1nW/3nW x Trans10/40/80) - post-campaign validation only

frozen: 2-D (FWHM, sigma_fit) kernel with per-dimension Scott exponent
Anuar's mu reward (loglik_mean) + sigma_prop score denominator
tunable: bandwidth_rule  choice  target | sim | power   (how H_F/H_S are computed)
h_f_scale       float   1.0 .. 12.0           (multiplier on the FWHM-channel bandwidth)
h_s_scale       float   1.0 .. 12.0           (multiplier on the sigma-channel bandwidth; floored)

bandwidth_rules.target: H = scale * std(real target) * N_target^(-1/6)  (exp5/exp6 design)
bandwidth_rules.sim: H = scale * std(sim cloud) * N_sim^(-1/6), recomputed every step (sim-adaptive)
bandwidth_rules.power: H = scale * std(pooled real targets of this laser power) * N^(-1/6)  (global / per-power)

protocol.success_bar: beat the experiment_6 level (objective ~0.086, best 0.0803) on the same T-weighted capped metric, with gamma finite on all 8 cells; the winner must ALSO hold on the 6 held-out experiments.
